name: Lumma Stealer (LummaC2) — ATT&CK Navigator Layer
description: MITRE ATT&CK mapping for Lumma Stealer (LummaC2) MaaS infostealer. Sources: CISA AA25-141B, Sophos, Netskope, Cybereason, ESET, CrowdStrike.

techniques.comment: Spearphishing attachments used to deliver Lumma payloads. Malicious ZIP/RAR files containing MSI loaders. Ref: CrowdStrike (2024), CISA AA25-141B.
Spearphishing hyperlinks redirect victims to malvertising pages and fake CAPTCHA sites. Ref: CISA AA25-141B.

ClickFix social engineering: fake CAPTCHA instructs victim to open Win+R, paste clipboard-injected PowerShell command. Victim executes the payload themselves. Ref: Netskope Threat Labs (Jan 2025), Sophos (2025).
Base64-encoded PowerShell one-liners used throughout infection chain. PowerShell fetches and executes staged payloads using System.Net.WebClient and Invoke-Expression (iex). Ref: Netskope, Qualys.
mshta.exe (signed Windows binary) used to download and execute remote HTA files containing obfuscated VBScript/JavaScript. Bypasses application controls. Ref: Cybereason, Picus Security (2025).
AMSI bypass: patches clr.dll in memory to force AmsiScanBuffer to return AMSI_RESULT_CLEAN. Open-source bypass implementation incorporated. Ref: Netskope Threat Labs (Jan 2025).
Sandbox/VM evasion: checks for AV process names ('wrsa', 'opssvc'), language settings, hardware fingerprint. Halts execution in sandbox environments. Ref: Picus Security, CISA AA25-141B.
C2 domain list hardcoded and encrypted in binary; decrypted at runtime. Payload sections RC4-encrypted (key: 656505). Multiple obfuscation layers in PowerShell stages. Ref: CISA AA25-141B.
Registry Run keys written to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run to maintain execution across reboots. Ref: AttackIQ, Cybereason.

Payload injected into RegSvcs.exe (legitimate signed Windows process) using memory allocation (VirtualAlloc) and shellcode writing. Disguises malicious activity under trusted process. Ref: Twilight Cyber, AttackIQ.
Session cookie exfiltration from Chromium/Firefox browsers. Stolen cookies bypass MFA and remain valid after password resets. Primary identity theft vector. Ref: CISA AA25-141B, Huntress.
Credentials from browser password stores targeted across Chromium and Firefox-based browsers. Username/password pairs, autofill data, credit card numbers. Ref: CISA AA25-141B, AttackIQ.
System information discovery at startup: OS version, architecture, language, CPU, RAM. Used to profile targets and filter out sandboxes/unwanted regions. Ref: CISA AA25-141B, AttackIQ.
File grabber functionality driven by C2 opcodes. Configurable file extensions and paths. Browser data collected for all Chromium/Firefox profiles. Ref: CISA AA25-141B (Opcode 0,1 analysis).

C2 communication via HTTP POST requests. User-agent 'TeslaBrowser/5.5'. Payload RC4-encrypted, LZNT1-compressed. Domains rotate across .shop/.top/.xyz/.store TLDs. Ref: CISA AA25-141B, ConnectWise CRU.
Ingress tool transfer: C2 Opcode 3 downloads additional files (payloads, modules) from attacker-specified URLs. GitHub abused for initial payload staging. Ref: CISA AA25-141B, Trend Micro (Jan 2025).
All stolen data exfiltrated over the established C2 channel (HTTP POST). Non-resident: without C2, no files written to disk. Ref: CISA AA25-141B.
